requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Executor confirmed no pre-existing appworker user (cmd-ea320c4a48ec47cc), created it with useradd -m (cmd-8b320a6fb4ef4b5e) showing uid=1000(appworker), and confirmed persistence post-restart via getent passwd (cmd-6ca6b37187be45d8).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files and 256 processes
requirements.summary: Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile=8192 and soft/hard nproc=256 (cmd-5ad06580d60d4155), verified enforcement via a real login shell showing ulimit -n=8192 and ulimit -u=256 (cmd-f9fbbb8789354382), and reconfirmed both the config content and live enforcement after a reboot (cmd-6ca6b37187be45d8).

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and configured a limits.d drop-in enforcing 8192 open files and 256 processes for its login sessions, verifying enforcement directly via a login shell both before and after a full reboot of node1. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was executed cleanly: baseline boot_id captured (bf4e9cbb...), reboot acknowledged via systemd-run, a new boot_id observed post-reconnect (3e520be2...), and account/config/enforcement re-verified afterward. Lifecycle snapshots show no unwanted residue or failed services. Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.
limitations: Only a single verification pass of ulimit values was captured before and after restart; no additional edge-case testing (e.g., attempting to exceed the limits) was performed, though this was not required by the task.
